summary: Observer post from 1910, steel tower built 1918, staffed to 1990, closed and derelict, restored by Friends and DEC, reopened September 2016 with summer stewards.

facts.design: 35-foot Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with a 7 x 7 ft metal cab

access.note: Reopened to the public on September 1, 2016 after restoration. The Friends group posts stewards on set days during the hiking season.

visit.trail_note: Hiking trail. The main trailhead is on Keese Mills Road; a lakeside trailhead is about 2.3 miles from the summit. NHLR's 2015 visit report says the trail is well marked but wet in some areas.

facts.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

events.note: Observer first stationed on St. Regis Mountain in April 1910; no tower was needed at first. NHLR dates the lookout site to 1909.
Fire fanned by swift winds on May 31, 1915 destroyed 1,550 acres of state land.
35-foot Aermotor LS40 steel tower erected by the state (Conservation Commission per the Friends history); still standing.
Staffed continuously through 1990 and closed at the end of the 1990 fire season.
Abandoned by DEC after closure; the tower began to deteriorate and the lower stairs were later removed.
Date registered May 1, 1995 per the NHLR detail page.
Placed on the New York State Register and the National Register of Historic Places in March 2005 (Wikipedia gives March 15, 2005).
In October 2010 the Adirondack Park Agency voted to classify the land beneath the St. Regis and Hurricane towers as historic, so the towers could stay and be restored.
Friends of St. Regis Mountain Fire Tower officially organized in May 2013.
DEC issued the final Unit Management Plan on November 7, 2014, allowing restoration to proceed.
Friends, volunteers and the Student Conservation Association installed railings, stairs, landings, safety fencing and a new cab floor in September 2015.
Restoration completed by the Friends and DEC; new roof flown up in July 2016; tower reopened to the public on September 1, 2016.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the site has hosted a lookout since 1909. The Friends history says an observer was first stationed in April 1910 and that no tower existed until 1918. The record uses April 1910 for the first observer and notes NHLR's 1909.

NHLR says the tower was staffed for 81 years before closing at the end of the 1990 fire season. The Friends history counts the era of organized detection as lasting 82 years, from 1910 to 1990. The story gives the dates and avoids the count.

A DEC fire-tower web page still says DEC and the Friends are restoring the tower so it can be opened. NHLR, the Friends history and the Adirondack Explorer all report a reopening to the public in September 2016. The story follows the 2016 reopening.
The Friends history says the listing came in March 2005. Wikipedia gives March 15, 2005. The record uses March 2005 and notes Wikipedia's exact date.

notes_for_editor: The Friends history is the main source and is a local-group account that cites Fred Knauf's history; the dates it gives for the observer, the 1918 tower, the 1990 closure, the 2014 management plan and the 2016 reopening agree with NHLR and the Adirondack Explorer. Open point: NHLR's 1909 site date versus the Friends' April 1910 observer date. The NRHP nomination PDF was not read. The Explorer's 6.6-mile round-trip figure from the main trailhead was not used. No photos were added; NHLR credits Bill Starr and David Petrelli for its photos, but their licences were not checked.
